code_commit_subject: fix(batch): emit the event replay reads, or the lift is structurally zero
how_determined: The batch process (PID 7952) was created at 21:12:46. f5d5288 was committed at 21:12:36, ten seconds earlier; the next commit, 63d9ace, landed at 21:14:39, after the process had started. A long-running process is pinned to the code it loaded, so this run is f5d5288 regardless of what HEAD later became.

equivalence_check.what_changed: d2d5301 tightened render() from a deny-list (too long / multi-line / ends a sentence) to an allow-list of per-variable kinds, after INC-010 showed 8 of 22 injection payloads riding through a template slot.
equivalence_check.unaffected: body_matches() does NOT apply the allow-list -- it calls _variable_problem() with no kind -- so every ledger row's body_matches_registered_template flag is still correct under HEAD. DLT-008 compliance is unchanged.
equivalence_check.affected: render() is stricter, so a proposal accepted under f5d5288 may be rejected under HEAD. The change can only convert model-decided into fallback; it cannot alter an accepted body's bytes.
equivalence_check.measured: 25 live proposals sampled from the same model with the same prompts: 4 accepted by both renderers, 21 accepted by f5d5288 only, 0 rejected by both.
equivalence_check.verdict: NOT EQUIVALENT. Under HEAD's renderer roughly 84% of this run's proposals would have fallen back, which exceeds MAX_TREATMENT_FALLBACK_RATE and would have INVALIDATED the run. The figure this batch produces belongs to f5d5288 and to no other commit.

known_defect_in_this_run.what: The model supplied amount="Rs 799" for a template reading "payment of Rs {#var#}", so every treatment message in this run renders as "payment of Rs Rs 799".
known_defect_in_this_run.why_it_was_invisible: The body still matched its registered template -- the slot accepted anything short and unpunctuated -- so body_matches_registered_template was True and DLT-008 passed.
known_defect_in_this_run.effect_on_the_lift_figure: NONE. SimTransport.execute() computes recovery from day_offset, channel, attempt_no and is_hard_decline. It does not read the body. Verified by inspecting the source.
known_defect_in_this_run.effect_on_the_claim: The run measures a system whose outbound copy was malformed, using a simulator blind to message quality. A real customer receiving "Rs Rs 799" would plausibly respond worse, so the simulated recovery rate is, if anything, generous to the treatment arm on this axis.
known_defect_in_this_run.fixed_in_head: The planner no longer accepts facts from the model. The amount, name and link are injected from context; anything the model sends under `variables` is discarded.

note: Written mid-run, before the figure existed, so the pinning is not a reconstruction. See CLAUDE.md section 4 for the standing rule.
